patches.old: - **Sebaceous glands** secrete sebum containing fatty acids and lactic acid that contribute to this acidic environment
patches.new: - **Sebaceous glands** secrete sebum whose free fatty acids, together with lactic acid from sweat, contribute to this acidic environment (the "acid mantle")
patches.reason: Lactic acid on the skin comes mainly from eccrine sweat, not sebum; sebum supplies free fatty acids.

patches.old: - **Peptidoglycan and lipoteichoic acid** — gram-positive bacterial cell wall components; detected by **TLR2**
patches.new: - **Lipoteichoic acid and bacterial lipoproteins** — cell-wall/envelope components (lipoteichoic acid is gram-positive); detected by **TLR2** (paired with TLR1 or TLR6). Peptidoglycan fragments are sensed mainly inside the cell by **NOD1/NOD2**
patches.reason: Purified peptidoglycan is sensed intracellularly by NOD1/NOD2; TLR2 activity of peptidoglycan preparations comes largely from contaminating LTA/lipoproteins.

patches.old: 1. **Phagocytosis and killing** — similar mechanisms to neutrophils, but macrophages are more efficient and longer-lived
patches.new: 1. **Phagocytosis and killing** — similar mechanisms to neutrophils; macrophages arrive later and have a weaker oxidative burst, but they are long-lived and can keep engulfing and killing for weeks to months
patches.reason: Conflicted with question 395, which correctly says neutrophils have the more potent oxidative burst.

patches.new:
- **Osteoclasts** — bone (bone resorption; formed by fusion of monocyte/macrophage-lineage cells)
- **Splenic and lymph node macrophages** — filter blood and lymph

(Glomerular **mesangial cells** can phagocytose, but they are smooth-muscle-like pericytes, not monocyte-derived macrophages.)
patches.reason: Mesangial cells are pericyte/smooth-muscle-like stromal cells, not tissue macrophages.

patches.old: the central region may undergo **caseous necrosis** (cheese-like appearance due to lipid-rich TB organisms)
patches.new: the central region may undergo **caseous necrosis** (dead cells are incompletely digested and clump into a soft, white, cheese-like mass)
patches.reason: The cheese-like appearance comes from incompletely digested necrotic cell debris, not from the organisms themselves.

patches.old: - **Lipoxins, resolvins, and protectins** — lipid mediators derived from arachidonic acid and omega-3 fatty acids that actively suppress inflammation and promote resolution
patches.new: - **Lipoxins** (from arachidonic acid) and **resolvins and protectins** (from the omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA) — lipid mediators that actively suppress inflammation and promote resolution
patches.reason: Makes the precursor of each family explicit: lipoxins come from arachidonic acid, resolvins and protectins from omega-3s.

patches.old: as well as lysosomal enzymes like myeloperoxidase.
patches.new: as well as granule enzymes; myeloperoxidase (from azurophilic granules) converts H₂O₂ to hypochlorous acid.
patches.reason: Myeloperoxidase is an azurophilic-granule enzyme that makes HOCl; clarified its role.

visual.title: The leukocyte adhesion cascade
visual.alt: A venule with blood flowing left to right over an endothelial lining. Neutrophils move through six steps: margination toward the wall; rolling as E- and P-selectins bind sialyl-Lewis X; activation as IL-8 on the endothelium signals through G-protein-coupled receptors to switch on integrins; firm adhesion of LFA-1 and Mac-1 (CD18) to ICAM-1; diapedesis between or through endothelial cells and across the basement membrane; and chemotaxis toward microbes along IL-8, C5a and fMLP gradients. A box notes that in leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1, missing CD18 blocks firm adhesion, giving high blood neutrophil counts, no pus and recurrent infections.
visual.caption: Selectins slow the cell, chemokines switch on integrins, and integrins stop it so it can cross.
